transcript: I went to go see Dear World at the New York City Center, so here are my thoughts. Dear World was the first show of this year's Encore series. And if you don't know what the encore series is, it's a series of 3 shows that the New York City Center puts on these elaborate staged concerts of every year for only about a week to 2 week long run. And Dear World was the perfect show to do in this series. This is a show that is rarely ever produced that I don't think is necessarily right for a full revival, but to bring it back to a New York stage for just a week was the perfect decision to make. Definitely put in the same vein of a Anyone Can Whistle or Floo Hooly where it's this very incredibly bizarre premise that deals with very, very real political and economic theme. In dear world, you have a businessman that wants to essentially blow up a cafe to get to the oil that is underneath it. But you also have, like, a love story and a mad woman dealing with the death of her husband. It is bizarre to say the least. Then you have these gorgeous musical theater songs that are just so traditional but belong to this very incredibly bizarre plot. Is written by Jerry Herman, who wrote Mame and Hello Dolly right before writing Dear World, and then Lacaja Fall right after. And this isn't my favorite score of His there's nothing that reaches the sheer perfection that is put on Your Sunday Clothes, but I really enjoyed a lot of these numbers and would definitely listen to a cast recording of this. And this cast was absolute perfection. Donna Murphy was in fact on book for the show. She did have COVID for the majority of the 10 day rehearsal period, but that didn't stop her from giving an absolutely brilliant performance. And in fact, in the past, encores! Productions used to be all on book. Also, Christopher Fitzgerald is just freaking hilarious. He had an entire scene in the second act that just had me rolling. So I am a New York City Center subscriber and this was my first time sitting in my new seat for the subscription, so this will be my seat for the rest of the season. I was in the balcony, which I also was for parade, so I was worried about this seat. I had absolutely no sightline issues, however. I'm literally 4th row in the balcony. It was absolutely perfect and the sound was great as well, which I was also worried about. My entire subscription was under $200, which made a lot more affordable for me and I get all 3 shows. I cannot recommend becoming a subscriber enough. It's really, really good deal. Really glad that encores! Chose to do Dear World. This is just such a weird show and while I know don't really feel like I need To see another production of it. I'm really glad that I saw this one. The next 2 shows in the season are Oliver and lighten the Piazza, which I cannot wait for both, but I'm really glad that they chose to do something as weird and bizarre as Dear World.
